sealed-ep8.name: student_capture + kld_report (sealed EP8 lane)

timing.provenance: ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED. No per-window wall clock was recorded for the sealed EP8 lane in a form this runner can cite. The figure is a deliberately conservative placeholder so the cost estimate errs high rather than low; the max-runtime coherence check uses it, and the printed estimate labels it. Replace it with a measured number from a sealed-lane run receipt.

notes: This is the lane K6 and Q4 were measured with, and the only one whose
flags are verified against the file in this checkout.  EP size is
env-driven (QP_GLM53_EP_SIZE) and the launcher's --nproc-per-node must
match it.  Requires the patched quant_pipeline tree (--pipeline-root)
and a BF16 skeleton carrying config.json + model.safetensors.index.json,
because the capture binds inventory.config_sha256/index_sha256 to the
LOCAL files.
--surface packed dereferences packed_root from the checkpoint's own
materialization-receipt.json.  For a third-party artifact that path is
on the producer's machine; see hfmeta.sniff_surface, which detects this
before any money is spent.
sealed-ep8.surfaces_note: student_capture.py --surface {packed,dione}, verified against the file. 'packed' additionally needs the payload store to be PUBLISHED in the repo; sniff_surface traps the case where the receipt's packed_root points at the producer's machine. There is no 'tr3-published' reader on THIS lane; the streaming lane gained one in M2 (stream_score --source tr3).

notes: Known properties from the validation run, which the receipt must disclose: bitwise
cross-topology parity is impossible (routed-expert combine order moves logits rms
0.26-0.28); streaming runs ARE bitwise identical to each other, so determinism holds
WITHIN the lane; peak 34-47 GB on one H200 as currently scheduled.
Inputs are THIS CAMPAIGN'S encode output (packed root with contract.json +
inventory.json + mtp-adapter-receipt.json + payload-store/{objects,choices}) plus a
--bf16 tree -- with the ONE exception of --source native (--inventory + --bf16 only).
at plan time, for $0.00 (see surfaces below).
NEW 2026-08-29: --capture-role teacher turns a native run into a SAME-LANE teacher
(engines/SAME-LANE-TEACHER.md); --store-positions per-window:<m> produces a PREVIEW
capture no sealed consumer accepts.

TR3-published is readable only after tr3_surface.verify_seal recomputes both receipt self-seals, metadata and name/count/scope bindings, and binds the shard map. Public K6 additionally requires exact pinned receipt/verdict bytes plus the sealed checkpoint identity bridge before decoding.
streaming.surfaces_note: stream_score.py --source {checkpoint,payload-store,dione,native,exl3hf,tr3}. 'packed' needs the payload store published; 'native-bf16' needs only --inventory + --bf16; 'exl3hf' reads a stock-exllamav3 HF-sharded release (mul1/mcg codebook, full-scope quant incl. quantized lm_head) and needs --bf16 pointing at the tree exl3hf_surface.py materialize produced from the SAME snapshot; 'tr3-published' reads a SEALED TR3 release (exl3-mcg, routed experts ONLY, native BF16 head) via tr3_surface; 'dione' reads an UNSEALED 0xSero selective-EXL3 release (exl3-mcg, routed experts of layers 3-44 only, TP4-sliced storage, everything else retained at source precision incl. the head) via dione_surface. tr3-published and dione both need --bf16 pointing at the non-routed tree their own materializer wrote from the SAME snapshot: their non-routed tensors ARE the official ones, but they cannot serve transformers out of the artifact's shards (tr3 interleaves them with routed payloads; dione's retained shards also carry the 864 MTP expert tensors) and transformers keys its checkpoint load off the shard FILES. || M5: 'gguf' reads a community llama.cpp container (--source gguf) via gguf_surface, whose dequant kernels are bitwise equal to gguf-py 0.19.0. It is the odd one out in this list twice over. (1) SCOPE: a GGUF quantizes the whole forward -- token_embd, lm_head, attention/KDA/DSA, shared experts, dense MLPs AND the routed experts -- so every measured weight is decoded from the artifact and NOTHING is retained at source precision; --bf16 narrows to the official config/tokenizer plus the vision tower, which the main GGUF does not carry (it ships as a separate mmproj file the text-only panel never executes). (2) IDENTITY: the repo is a SHELF, not an artifact -- unsloth publishes twelve builds of GLM-5.3-Flash at one revision -- so a measurement names a build with --path and the receipt carries that build's file list with whole-file sha256, not just the repo revision.

8.0.detail: Pinned K8 publishes a self-sealed materialization receipt, ABI, shard map and stream-k8-kld summary, but no pinned verdict or other recomputable receipt binds the measured student checkpoint identity and asserts it scored the sealed K8 surface. K6 evidence is not transferable.

bitwise identical to CPU (selftest_decode_parity).  fp64 KLD accumulation cannot
run on MPS at all; the scorer (bin/kld_preview.py) pins it to CPU and says so.

bf16-floor.name: stream_score --source native (the lane's BF16 measurement floor)

timing.provenance: MEASURED on 1x H200 spot (IN2, 28 vCPU, 300 GiB cgroup) reading the 599 GB BF16 tree off a CephFS filesystem at ~1.05 GB/s with 28 reader threads: window 1 (cold, all 42 layers filled) 678 s; steady-state windows 483-549 s with --decode-cache ram holding 17 of 42 layers. See engines/BF16-FLOOR.md.

notes: This lane does not score a quant. It scores the UN-QUANTIZED BF16 experts through the
identical capture, so its panel mean is the FLOOR every quant measured on this lane
sits on top of. Subtract it (engines/tools/bf16_floor_summary.py) to state a quant's
quantization-attributable error.
It is the only stream_score source that needs NO packed root: --inventory (a sealed
quant-pipeline.glm-release-inventory.v1) plus the --bf16 tree is the whole input.
It is IO-bound, not decode-bound: 14.50 GB of routed BF16 per layer, 42 layers per
window. Size the box by filesystem read bandwidth and by 47.1 GB of VRAM, not by
matmul throughput.
Requires SM90-class or newer ONLY in the sense that the venv is pinned to torch
2.11.0+cu130; an instance whose driver predates CUDA 13 cannot run it at all
(observed on an A100-80GB image shipping driver 12080).
The workspace symlink farm (/workspace/artifacts/...) must exist before the run: the
sealed panel receipt declares those paths and the artifact identity check refuses
symlinked FILES while requiring the directories to resolve.
bf16-floor.surfaces_note: The official BF16 release tree itself (config.json + model.safetensors.index.json + shards). Not a reader for a third-party quant.
